question: Which of the following reactions occurs, - when the exchange of two ions takes place?
solution:
The correct answer is __**double displacement reaction**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In a double displacement reaction,** two compounds exchange ions to form two new compounds.**
 
• These reactions typically occur in aqueous solutions where ions are free to move.
 
• Double displacement reactions can result in the formation of a precipitate, gas, or weak electrolyte.
 
• An example of a double displacement reaction is the reaction between silver nitrate (AgNO₃) and sodium chloride (NaCl) to form silver chloride (AgCl) and sodium nitrate (NaNO₃).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Displacement Reaction**

 
 
• Involves the replacement of one element in a compound by another element.
 
• Example: Zn + CuSO₄ → ZnSO₄ + Cu.
 
 
 
• **Decomposition Reaction**
 
 
• A single compound breaks down into two or more simpler substances.
 
• Example: 2H₂O → 2H₂ + O₂.
 
 
 
• **Combination Reaction**
 
 
• Two or more substances combine to form a single compound.
 
• Example: 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O.
 
 
 
• **Precipitate Formation**
 
 
• It occurs when a solid forms from a solution during a chemical reaction.
 
• The solid is called the precipitate.
